Solution.S:
Given $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & \tan x \\ -\tan x & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

Then $A^T = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -\tan x \\ \tan x & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

$|A| = 1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x$, so $A^{-1} = \frac{1}{\sec^2 x} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -\tan x \\ \tan x & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \cos^2 x \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -\tan x \\ \tan x & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

Thus $A^T A^{-1} = \cos^2 x \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -\tan x \\ \tan x & 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -\tan x \\ \tan x & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

Multiply:

First row, first column: $1 \cdot 1 + (-\tan x)(\tan x) = 1 - \tan^2 x$
First row, second column: $1 \cdot (-\tan x) + (-\tan x) \cdot 1 = -2\tan x$
Second row, first column: $(\tan x) \cdot 1 + 1 \cdot (\tan x) = 2\tan x$
Second row, second column: $(\tan x)(-\tan x) + 1 \cdot 1 = 1 - \tan^2 x$

So $A^T A^{-1} = \cos^2 x \begin{bmatrix} 1 - \tan^2 x & -2\tan x \\ 2\tan x & 1 - \tan^2 x \end{bmatrix}$.

Using $\cos^2 x = \frac{1}{1+\tan^2 x}$, we get:

$\cos^2 x (1 - \tan^2 x) = \frac{1 - \tan^2 x}{1 + \tan^2 x} = \cos 2x$

$\cos^2 x (-2\tan x) = -\frac{2\tan x}{1 + \tan^2 x} = -\sin 2x$

$\cos^2 x (2\tan x) = \frac{2\tan x}{1 + \tan^2 x} = \sin 2x$

Thus $A^T A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \cos 2x & -\sin 2x \\ \sin 2x & \cos 2x \end{bmatrix}$, which corresponds to option B.
